messages:
ashley: heads up — after yesterday's RBAC refactor i ran a quick audit and found several users still able to decrypt with our default KMS key even though they were removed from crypto-admin via SCIM. not sure if this is a SCIM delta issue or a grant leftover. anyone seen this?

mike: which key and which users? example pls.

ashley: key: projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/primary/crypto-default. user example: svc-ingest@partner (was removed from group 'crypto-admins' at 2026-03-18T22:14Z). verified via app logs — decrypt calls succeed.

julia: hm. did SCIM emit a deprovision event? check scim-provisioner logs and the kafka topic. last deploy touched group-rename migration. @mike can you pull scim consumer offset?

mike: pull started. quick look: scim consumer shows a PATCH for svc-ingest to remove group, consumer successfully acked at 2026-03-18T22:15Z. provisioning service returned 200.

ashley: so SCIM did the removal. suspect is either the KMS grant wasn't revoked, or there's a role binding cached somewhere (we have shadow-membership cache in auth-proxy).

devops-bot: deploy:rbac-refactor v2 rolled at 2026-03-18T21:50Z by @deploy-bot. Post-deploy hook: auth-cache-flush scheduled.

mike: can we check KMS grants? for AWS KMS: `aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/crypto-default` — see if there's a grant referencing the principal. also check IAM inline policies on service-role that might include wildcard.

julia: adding quick repro snippet i ran locally:
```
# Query auth-proxy cache
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://auth-proxy.internal/_debug/shadow-memberships?user=svc-ingest@partner
# Expected: empty list
# Actual: ["crypto-admins"]
```

security-oncall: tagging incident triage. this looks like permission drift. severity = P2 unless we find evidence of active misuse. recommended immediate steps: 1) revoke active KMS grants for affected principals, 2) invalidate auth-proxy cache, 3) run SCIM reconcile (full sync) for tenant, 4) preserve logs for forensics.

sam: i can revoke the grant. before i do, can we back up the grant ids and contexts? run `aws kms list-grants` and `aws kms get-grant-token`? i'll snapshot. planning to revoke in next 10m.

mike: also check the role mapping layer that translates SCIM groups -> IAM roles. we recently added an alias mapping for group rename (crypto-admins -> crypto-operators). if the mapping was applied in the wrong direction during the refactor it could have left an alias grant.

ashley: good call. i pulled the mapping table and found a stale alias entry: { "crypto-admins": "crypto-operators" } but it was inverted in the migration script for a short window. that lines up with the window when svc-ingest was removed.

sam: snapshot saved. revoking grants now: `aws kms retire-grant --grant-id <id>` ... done for 3 grants referencing svc-ingest. responses: 200. confirmed via `list-grants` those entries gone.

devops-bot: action:auth-cache-flush executed by @mike at 2026-03-19T00:12Z

mike: flushed auth-proxy cache and restarted the consumer that applies SCIM deltas. verified curl debug shows empty shadow-memberships for svc-ingest now.

julia: running full SCIM reconcile for tenant (started). i'll post results.

security-oncall: keep an eye on any failed decrypts from production ingestion. if we see noise, roll a short mitigation: deny-list the old grant principals at the KMS policy layer. also file a postmortem if root cause is migration script inversion.

ashley: thanks all. tentative root cause: migration script inverted alias mapping -> leftover grants + cache not invalidated in time. followups: (1) add preflight for migration scripts to validate mapping direction, (2) add automated KMS grant cleanup as part of group rename, (3) add integration test that runs SCIM remove -> KMS grant revocation path. i'll open JIRA and link here.

sam: i'll paste grant ids/backup into the ticket and attach snapshots.

julia: reconcile finished: removed 12 stale memberships across 4 users, no other keys affected.

ashley: closing this thread for now. will update ticket with postmortem draft. :thumbsup:
